properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 2014-09-02 to Exco Resources Pa Llc in Cherryhill Twp, Indiana county. 78.66BRINE - Failure to report a reportable release of brine to DEP within 2 hours.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Exco Resources Pa Llc
Violation Type Administrative
Violation Date 2014-09-02
Violation Code 78.66BRINE - Failure to report a reportable release of brine to DEP within 2 hours.
Violation ID 704020
Permit API 063-35906
Unconventional N
County Indiana
Municipality Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date 2014-09-02
Comments SPILL. A release of 4.5 bbl brine water was reported to SWRO at 1424 by Opr rep Dan Chimino.Release discovered at 1050.No waterways reported to be affected. UPDATE: 9/3/14 Upon receipt of spill report, Dept contacted Mr.Chimino at 0750 via phone.Mr. Chimino stated that 4.5 bbl brine released into dike due to leaking bolt on brine tank.Fluids removed from tank and dike on 9/2 and contractor will be on-site today to further remediation efforts. Mr. Chimino stated that release discovered on 9/2 at 1050. Dept was not notified of this release until 1424. Per current regs, if a reportable release of brine on or into ground occurs at the well site, the Opr shall notify the appropriate regional office of Dept as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hrs after detecting the release. Hence, this release was not reported to Dept w/in regulated timeframe.Viols being issued for failure to notify Dept w/in 2 hrs after discovering a reportable release of brine onto ground.A FUI will be conducted to assess any envir'l impacts and/or issue viols as necessary.

Comments: On 06/16/2025, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the HIXENBAUGH 1-P060 OG well in West Bethlehem Township, Washington County. The following was observed during inspection:-I observed a slope failure 90x5 ft along access road to well site. The slope failure was found by the Department and not reported. The toe of the slope failure is within access road drainage channel (Photo 1-5). On 04/17/2024 (SAIR 3741762) and 05/10/2024 (SAIR 3760574) stabilization and remediation to access road and channel slope was conducted.-I observed erosion rills and ruts along the access road. I recommend maintenance to access road (Photo 6 and 7).-A well tag was observed on the well head. Some corrosion was observed on well head (Photo 8 and 9).-The well and operator's information were displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h) (Photo 10).-Some corrosion was observed on the production equipment. It appears production equipment was leaking. No elevated conductivity fluid was observed (Photo 11 and 12).-I observed Low Ash Gas Engine Oil/fuel appears to be leaking onto the ground below next to compressor station. I recommend remediation and maintenance to well site (Photo 13-17,20).-Some corrosion was observed on the production tank (Photo 18 and 19).Determination:Violations are being issued for slope failure along access road: 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1, and 78.53. Violations are being issued for fuel leaking onto well site. The operator failed to report: 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.54, and SWMA 301

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/29/2025 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Jackson Township, Tioga county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/29/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8260073
Permit API: 117-20391
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Jackson Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/29/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Barrett 410 well pad located in Jackson Township, Tioga County on 12/29/2025 at 1025 hours. The weather was 41 degrees F with mostly cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator.On 12/24/2025, Repsol reported to the DEP via the reporting hotline that an estimated 23 gallons of produced fluids were released to the soil/gravel after the dump line for the produced fluids separated. Repsol reported that the impacted soil/gravel was recovered and that a third party company would visit on Friday, 12/26/2025, to verify that cleanup was complete. During my inspection, evidence of remediation was observed off the western fill slope (photo #6). Impacted materials were placed in a lined and covered residual waste container stored onsite (photo #2). The dump line appears to have a temporary repair in place (photo #5) with tape over the damage line. A bucket is located below the line to collect any additional leaks. Repsol reported that a permanent repair is scheduled for the near future. Any fluids and soils in and around the remediated area showed no evidence of any portion of the release remaining. Based on the findings of this inspection report, the reported release of produced fluids outside of secondary containment and Repsol's timely remediation, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-20391:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)SWMA 301I departed the site at 1135 hours.

Comments: On 10/27/23 at 12:40 I, along with OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted a routine inspection of the well. The Act 9 sign was present, but faded. DEP recommends a new sign is erected. A review of documents shows the ERP was updated in February of 2023 and provided to DEP. The well posting and tag were present and legible. The well appeared to be shut in and not in production. A review of APRs indicated the well last produced in September 2022. The well is abandoned as defined in chapter 32. Violations of 3220 and 78A91 are being issued. DEP requests a schedule for when the well will be plugged or placed in production. MIA reports are current. Brine tank 1 appeared heavily corroded and what appeared to be holes were forming in the tank wall. A violation of 78A57d has resulted and DEP requests 12 months of brine tank inspections. Brine tank 2 appeared to be in sound condition. Secondary containment for brine tank 1 and 2 appeared sufficiently maintained to manage precipitation accumulation and to ensure containment integrity. A condensate/brine tank was present that was not situated within secondary containment. The tank appeared to be less than 1320 gallons. The tank was not grounded in violation of 78a56(a)10

Inspection Date: 3/11/2024
Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Heavy sedimentation was observed in the access road, with accelerated erosion rills observed in the access road closer to the well pad (see photos 2 and 3). Flowback equipment and related secondary containment was removed from site, as well as the rolloff dumpsters containing the impacted material (see photo 4). GPU units onsite were either placed within secondary containment or equipped with interconnected vertical separators (see photo 6). The area formerly impacted by the spill documented in IR 3737318 and IR 3736812 was freshly backfilled with no elevated conductivity detected (see photos 7-10). The ERP was onsite (see photo 10). Well 4H was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). Violations issued under IR 3737318 shall remain outstanding, as the NOI to Remediation of the release under Act 2 requirements have not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB Program. Additional violations are being issued against the accelerated erosion and heavy sedimentation observed in the access road.

Inspection Date: 7/23/2026
Comments: On July 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4209208, where violations were continued for broken and corroded piping causing a release, as well as the issuance of new violations for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.Accompanying on today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4209208, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it, however the well tag does not appear to updated and the phone number listed on the tag is not in service. Violations are being continued at this time for having inaccurate information on the well tag/posting. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank ((3.80 mS and Over Range (>12mS)) and adjacent to the broken corroded pipe (0.329 mS). These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil conductivity reading of 0.181 mS collected upslope and away from the release area. The soil conductivity readings in the release area are elevated compared to background subjugating that the release from the back of the production tank on the right has yet to be remediated. Violations are being continued at this time for the release from the production tank.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. The Department is again requesting the Operator provide the Department with a Notice of Violation Operator response within 14 days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping, inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site is to remain outstanding at this time.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 977493
Permit API: 105-21923
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Ulysses Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/30/2022
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM - Headwaters 146 Well Pad located in Ulysses Twp, Tioga Co on 11/30/22 @1300 hours in response to a release of between 5 and 42 gallons of completions fluid into secondary containment and onto the pad surface. The weather was 45 degrees, rain, winds W @15mph. Terra Tokarz, JKLM Env Field Coordinator was present onsite. JKLM was in the process of dewatering a transfer line into the frack tanks when a cam lock on the hose failed. Mrs. Tokarz stated the majority of the fluid was captured by the tank secondary containment, but a revised estimate of 10 gallons was released to the pad surface in a spray. The impacted area was approximately 15' x 30" off the back side of the frack tanks. Approximately 1" of pad material was removed from the impacted area and placed in a dump truck on secondary containment until a waste container could be procured. The area was screened for field conductivity and found to be <1.0mS/cm. Elevated fluid was still located in the secondary containment. Mrs. Tokarz stated the vacuum truck onsite is routinely removing the fluid from the secondary containment. JKLM stated they had screened the pad E and S controls and no elevated conductivity was found. Due to conditions onsite observed during this inspection, it appears the spill has been adequately remediated.Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against the 2HU (API#105-21923) well:25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)SWMA 301CSL 402(b)I departed the site at 1430

Permit API: 083-57192
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Sergeant Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/02/2020
Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill at the Burning Well PV-81 well site on December 2nd at 9:20 am. The Complaint ID for this spill is #353829.A tree near the well fell due to heavy snow and wind overnight onto the lead line of the well, causing a union to fail. The well is pumped with an electric powered pumpjack that is on a timer. This well begins to pump at 8:00 am. At 8:30 am, the well pumper came by and found the well leaking. He immediately shut the well in and informed the operator of the spill. The tree was cut off the line and the flow of oil was stopped. Dave Hill plus two well pumpers from PVE were on site when I arrived, as were three representatives of Howard Drilling, who had been called to help clean the oil up. They were using a portable vacuum tank to collect any loose oil they could find. The oil appears to be caught in the snow in an area approximately 15-20 feet circular down gradient from the spot of the leak. No oil flowed outside this area, as heavy snow acted to slow and prevent seepage. It appears as though 10-20 gallons of crude oil was spilled from the compromised line. The operator has cleared the top of the tree from this area to begin cleanup. Snow and debris have been cleared at the edge of the contaminated area. The operator has placed a continuous pile of absorbent peat in this cleared area around the spill as a berm. They intend to rake and shovel the oily snow and debris to the center of the area, then load it into two or more plastic totes that will be used as temporary storage. The entire area will then be covered again with peat for the time being. When conditions allow, they intend to dig up any soil that is contaminated and haul it to the landfill, along with the oil covered sticks from the site. Continued inspection will be performed on this site as cleanup progresses. See attached sheet for violations.

Comments: On November 26, 2019, I conducted a follow up inspection related to a release of material reported to the Department on 11/23/2019. I was accompanied by PADEP OGI John Rushin and Range Resources representatives Nate Smiell, John Fountain. Nick Reda and Matthew Kravitis. At the time of inspection, the impacted area was excavated to an approximated depth of 7 feet. The excavated area was approximately 30'x25'. I was able to see all sides of the corrugated steel well cellar and surrounding bed rock material. It appears that the impacted material has been removed but will be confirmed with sampling as the Operator continues to follow the spill policy. I did observe a significant crack in the bedrock below the 5H cellar. Mr. Smiell measured the crack and it was found to be approximately 79” in length and approximately 15” deep. The crack was approximately 2” wide. This could be a potential pathway to groundwater and the Operator should continue to monitor the key way drains and surface waters as a precaution. Additionally, the Operator has updated the amount of OBM released from 3 barrels to 5 barrels. The impacted material removed from the well pad was placed in 15 roll off boxes awaiting disposal. PADEP John Rushin was onsite and discussed additional issued related to the cement returns with the 5H and 6H wells. Violations remain outstanding and additional violations may be forthcoming as part of the Departments investigation.

Comments: On 3/18/21 at 1153 hrs., I conducted an inspection of DiversifiedProduction, LLC's F Kinter 3 well (API 063-35436) in Center Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of 42.5 barrels of production fluid onto the ground from a tank located onsite. According to the operator, corroded threads on a coupling connected to the tank was the cause of the release. Photos were submitted to the Department prior to inspection of the site. The release impacted the earthen berm containment area and a portion of an agricultural field to the north of the berm. Conductivity readings were elevated both within the earthen berm and outside the berm, indicating migration through the berm and soil in the adjacent field. The operator had tentatively delineated the northern extent of the migration with yellow flags. Soil conductivity beyond the northern most flag was at background level. The operator notified the Department that remediation of the site would commence on Monday, 3/22/21. The release of production fluids from a tank onto the ground constitutes violations of SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and 78.57(a). The violations associated with this release will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to Page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release and demonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.
